Meat / Restaurant

Jumulleok Sesame-Garlic Steak Bites

Jumulleok means "hand-mixed" — cubed steak tossed in seasoning minutes before it hits the fire, not hours.

Korean · Easy · Serves 3–4

Jump to recipe ↓
Chapter 01 / 20 meat recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: restaurant, the instant-toss clock. Jumulleok means "hand-mixed" — cubed steak tossed in seasoning minutes before it hits the fire, not hours. It is the Gwangyang school of timing (#M08's dry-grate cousin logic, applied to cubes): the juice stays inside the meat because the marinade never had time to pull it out. Of everything on this site, this is the fastest route from the butcher to the table — ten minutes of prep, a hot grate, and the seasoning bowl right at the grill so the next batch can be tossed while the first one cooks. Who cooks what: the seasoning bowl lives at the grill boss's station. Toss, grill, repeat.

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • The whole method is the clock: the toss happens when the grill is ready, not before. Cube the meat, keep it cold, mix the toss ingredients in a bowl set beside the grill. Sesame oil, soy, garlic, salt, pepper — nothing needs to dissolve, which is exactly why no marinating time is needed.
  • Get the grate genuinely hot first. The cubes need a hard sear in the 90 seconds a side they get; a lukewarm grate is the only way this recipe fails.
  • While the first batch grills: the raw cubes stay in the fridge, not on the counter. Hand-mixed at the last second is a technique, not a reason to hold raw meat at room temperature.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Toss the first batch: meat into the bowl, hands or tongs, thirty seconds of turning until every cube wears the mix. Onto the hot grate with a finger's width between cubes — crowded cubes steam gray. Checkpoint — the cubes should hit with an aggressive sizzle and the sesame-garlic smell should rise immediately. No sizzle, no sear — pull the batch back and let the grate recover.
  2. 02
    Grill 90 seconds undisturbed, turn each cube to a new face, another 90 seconds, then roll to the last faces for 30–60 seconds. Total cook: about 4 minutes for medium at 3 cm. Pull when the faces are browned and the cube feels softly springy at a finger press. Checkpoint — cut one open at the grill station: a thin browned crust and a rosy interior. Gray to the center means the grate was too cool or the cubes too big — 3 cm is the ceiling.
  3. 03
    Sesame seeds over, warm platter, straight to the table. Toss the next batch while the table eats this one — the rhythm of the record is toss, grill, eat, repeat, and the meat is at its best in the first minute off the fire. Checkpoint — eating test: crust, juice, sesame. The center should taste of beef and black pepper more than soy — if it reads salty, the soy ran a teaspoon heavy; the toss is measured in grams for a reason. Chef’s Note — why the last-second toss works better than it should: salt and soy begin pulling moisture out of meat within minutes, but for the first ten or fifteen the exchange mostly runs the other way — surface seasoning in, minimal juice out. Cook inside that window and you get seasoned crust and un-drained beef simultaneously. It is the same juice-stays-in-the-sheet logic the Gwangyang grill houses run at the ticket window, and it is why jumulleok cubes taste juicier than the same meat marinated for an afternoon.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cubes gray, no crustGrate not hot enough or cubes crowdedPreheat harder; finger-width spacing
Salty bitesSoy over-measured or double-dipped in gireumjangWeigh the toss; salt the dip lighter
Interior overcookedCubes under 3 cm or grilled to a clock3 cm cubes; press-test, not timer
Garlic scorched bitterGrated garlic on the hottest grate zoneToss cubes in the bowl, tap off excess before grilling

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • This is a cook-and-eat record; the toss doesn't hold. Leftover cooked cubes keep 2 days and make the best fried rice in this whole category — the sesame-garlic crust re-toasts beautifully in a hot pan.
  • Variations: a teaspoon of gochugaru in the toss for slow heat; butter and a splash of soy in the last minute for a glaze finish; the same toss on a whole sliced skirt steak, grilled as sheets, is the fastest cousin of #M01 without the slurry.
